title: Windows launchers should not spawn visible PowerShell shells
symptoms: Repeated PowerShell windows appear when background helpers or startup fallbacks launch
Minimized shells still interrupt operator work on Windows desktops
root_cause: A background daemon repeatedly invoked powershell.exe for liveness checks and recovery, but the subprocesses were not always created with CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows.
fix: Start the actual worker with pythonw.exe or a detached subprocess when possible
Use a hidden launcher such as WScript.Shell.Run(..., 0, False) for startup-folder fallbacks
Avoid -WindowStyle Minimized as a substitute for true hiding
When Task Scheduler resists direct PowerShell actions, point the task at pythonw.exe and let a Python wrapper launch PowerShell with CREATE_NO_WINDOW
Apply CREATE_NO_WINDOW directly inside the shell worker and GUI backend subprocess helpers
notes: The active popup source was the old factory_daemon.py process; restarting it after adding CREATE_NO_WINDOW removed the visible PowerShell child process path.
A child powershell.exe with command line 'Get-Process -Id <pid> | Out-Null' is expected on Windows, but it should now run hidden.
